question:
Article 126 of the Indian Constitution mentions _____________.

[SSC GD 2024]
options: Appointment of acting Chief Justice of India
Supreme Court to be a court of record
Seat of Supreme Court
Appointment of ad hoc Judges
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Appointment of acting Chief Justice of India

Explanation:
Article 126 of the Indian Constitution deals with the 'Appointment of acting Chief Justice of India'. It states that if the office of the Chief Justice of India (CJI) is vacant or the CJI is unable to perform duties, the President may appoint the senior-most judge of the Supreme Court as the acting CJI until a regular appointment is made. This ensures the continuity of judicial functions.

Extra Facts:
- The appointment of the CJI is governed under Article 124.
- Article 127 provides for the appointment of ad hoc judges when there is a lack of quorum in the Supreme Court.
- Article 129 declares the Supreme Court as a 'Court of Record', whose judgments serve as legal precedents.

question:
Article 22 of the Indian Constitution is related to which of the following?

[SSC CHSL 2023]
options: Right to education
Protection of personal liberty
Preventive detention
Protection of life
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Preventive detention

Explanation:
Article 22 of the Indian Constitution deals with 'Protection against arrest and detention' and 'Preventive detention'. It provides certain safeguards related to arrest and detention:
1. Right to be informed of the grounds of arrest (Article 22(1)).
2. Right to be produced before a magistrate within 24 hours (Article 22(2)).
3. Special provisions for preventive detention laws (Article 22(3) to 22(7)).
Preventive detention allows arresting a person to prevent them from committing a crime, rather than as punishment. It is used in the interest of public order or national security.

Extra Facts:
◼ Preventive Detention Act is mentioned in Article 22(4) to 22(7).
◼ Article 22(3) excludes criminals or enemy aliens from these protections.
◼ Article 22(5) mandates that the detained person must be informed of the detention grounds.
◼ Article 22(7) empowers Parliament to make preventive detention laws.
◼ In AK Gopalan Case (1950), SC held that Article 22 is not an exception to Article 21.

Expected Questions for Upcoming Exams :
☛ Which article protects 'personal liberty' in the Indian Constitution? → Article 22
☛ What is the maximum period of preventive detention without approval? → 3 months
☛ Article 22 is part of which Fundamental Right? → Right to Freedom (Articles 19-22)
☛ Where can appeals against preventive detention be filed? → Advisory Board
☛ What is the detention period under Article 22(4)? → 2 months (without Advisory Board approval)
question_hi:
भारतीय संविधान का अनुच्छेद 22 निम्नलिखित में से किससे संबंधित है?

[SSC CHSL 2023]
options_hi: शिक्षा का अधिकार
दैहिक स्वतंत्रता का संरक्षण
निवारक निरोध
जीवन का संरक्षण
solution_hi:
हल: सही उत्तर है निवारक निरोध

Explanation:
भारतीय संविधान का अनुच्छेद 22 'दैहिक स्वतंत्रता का संरक्षण' और 'निवारक निरोध' से संबंधित है। यह अनुच्छेद गिरफ्तारी और निरोध से संबंधित कुछ मौलिक सुरक्षा उपाय प्रदान करता है। इसमें तीन प्रावधान शामिल हैं:
1. गिरफ्तार किए गए व्यक्ति को गिरफ्तारी के कारणों से अवगत कराना (अनुच्छेद 22(1))।
2. गिरफ्तार व्यक्ति को 24 घंटे के भीतर निकटतम मजिस्ट्रेट के सामने पेश करना (अनुच्छेद 22(2))।
3. निवारक निरोध कानूनों के तहत गिरफ्तारी की विशेष प्रक्रिया (अनुच्छेद 22(3) से 22(7))।
निवारक निरोध का उद्देश्य किसी व्यक्ति को अपराध करने से पहले ही गिरफ्तार करना है, न कि सजा देना। यह सार्वजनिक व्यवस्था या राष्ट्रीय सुरक्षा के हित में लागू किया जाता है।

Extra Facts:
◼ निवारक निरोध अधिनियम (Preventive Detention Act) का उल्लेख अनुच्छेद 22(4) से 22(7) में किया गया है।
◼ अनुच्छेद 22(3) में अपराधी या शत्रु विदेशियों को इस सुरक्षा से छूट दी गई है।
◼ अनुच्छेद 22(5) के अनुसार, निरोधित व्यक्ति को निरोध के आधारों से अवगत कराया जाना चाहिए।
◼ अनुच्छेद 22(7) संसद को निवारक निरोध कानून बनाने का अधिकार देता है।
◼ AK गोपालन केस (1950) में SC ने कहा कि अनुच्छेद 22, अनुच्छेद 21 का अपवाद नहीं है।

question:
Which Article of the Indian Constitution states that “There shall be a High Court for each state” ?

[SSC CPO 2024]
options: Article 275
Article 245
Article 214
Article 125
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Article 214

Explanation:
Article 214 of the Indian Constitution explicitly states that "There shall be a High Court for each state." This provision falls under Part VI (The States) of the Constitution and defines the structure of the judiciary at the state level. The High Court is the highest judicial authority in a state and is established by the Constitution. Apart from Article 214, Article 215 grants High Courts the status of a 'Court of Record', meaning their judgments have legal sanctity and can be cited as evidence in future cases.

Extra Facts:
- Article 231 empowers Parliament to establish a common High Court for two or more states (e.g., Punjab & Haryana High Court).
- Currently, India has 25 High Courts, some of which have jurisdiction over multiple states/UTs.
- Judges of the High Court are appointed by the President in consultation with the Chief Justice of India and the Governor of the concerned state (Article 217).

Expected Questions for Upcoming Exams :
☛ How many High Courts are there in India? → 25
☛ Who appoints the judges of the High Court? → The President
☛ Which Article declares the High Court as a 'Court of Record'? → Article 215
☛ Under which Article can Parliament establish a common High Court for multiple states? → Article 231

question:
Article 26 of the Indian constitution is related with which of the following?

[SSC CHSL 2022]
options: Non-payment of religious taxes
Freedom to manage religious affairs
Freedom as to payment of taxes for promotion of any particular religion
Protection of interests of minorities
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Freedom to manage religious affairs

Explanation:
Article 26 of the Indian Constitution deals with the 'Freedom to manage religious affairs'. It grants religious denominations the following rights:
1. To establish and maintain institutions for religious and charitable purposes.
2. To manage their own religious affairs.
3. To own and acquire movable and immovable property.
4. To administer such property in accordance with the law.
This right is part of the Fundamental Right to Freedom of Religion (Articles 25-28), subject to public order, morality, and health.

Extra Facts:
1. Article 25 relates to individual religious freedom, while Article 26 concerns the rights of religious institutions.
2. Article 27 prohibits compulsory taxation for the promotion of any particular religion.
3. Article 28 restricts religious instruction in state-funded educational institutions.
4. These provisions uphold India's secular character.

☛ What does Article 27 prohibit? → Compulsory taxes for religious promotion
☛ What is restricted under Article 28? → Religious instruction in state-funded institutions
☛ Which article protects minority educational institutions? → Article 30

question:
Who among the following shall communicate to the President all the decisions of the Council of Ministers under article 78?

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options: Home minister
Prime Minister
Vice President
Foreign minister
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Prime Minister

Explanation:
Under Article 78 of the Indian Constitution, it is the duty of the Prime Minister to communicate all decisions of the Council of Ministers and legislative proposals to the President. This provision ensures a constitutional relationship between the President and the Council of Ministers. The President, as the constitutional head of the country, is kept informed about government decisions by the Prime Minister, who heads the Council of Ministers. This process maintains transparency and accountability in government functioning.

Extra Facts:
- Article 74 provides for a Council of Ministers to aid and advise the President, and the President acts on their advice.
- The 42nd Constitutional Amendment (1976) clarified that the President shall act in accordance with the advice of the Council of Ministers.
- Article 75 deals with the appointment of the Prime Minister and the functions of ministers.

question:
Which Article of the Constitution of India deals with the conduct of business of the Government of a state ?

[SSC CGL 2024]
options: Article 177
Article 167
Article 164
Article 166
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Article 166

Explanation:
Article 166 of the Indian Constitution deals with the conduct of business of the Government of a state. This article specifies the procedure regarding the transaction of business by the Governor of a state. It states that all executive actions of the state government are taken in the name of the Governor, but the real power lies with the Council of Ministers. Decisions of the state government are formally notified and authenticated by ministers under this article. This provision is analogous to Article 77, which governs the conduct of business of the Central Government.

Extra Facts:
- Article 167 outlines the duties of the Chief Minister, including keeping the Governor informed about administrative decisions.
- Article 164 deals with the appointment, removal, and oath of state ministers.
- Article 177 grants privileges to ministers (who are MLAs), such as the right to speak on budgetary matters.

question:
Which Article of the Constitution of India deals with the conduct of business of the Government of a state ?

[SSC CGL 2024]
options: Article 177
Article 167
Article 164
Article 166
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Article 166

Explanation:
Article 166 of the Indian Constitution deals with the conduct of business of the Government of a state. This article specifies the procedure regarding the transaction of business by the Governor of a state. It states that all executive actions of the state government are taken in the name of the Governor, but the real power lies with the Council of Ministers. This provision is analogous to Article 77, which governs the conduct of business of the Central Government.

Establishment of NTA
Establishment of SSC

solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Establishment of UPSC and SPSC

Explanation:
Article 315 of the Indian Constitution deals with the establishment of Public Service Commissions for the Union and States. It states:
- A Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) for the Union, and
- A State Public Service Commission (SPSC) for each State.
This article is part of Part XIV (Articles 308-323) of the Constitution, which pertains to 'Services'. The primary role of UPSC and SPSC is to conduct examinations for recruitment to various posts under the Central and State Governments.

Extra Facts:
- Article 316 outlines the appointment and tenure of Commission members.
- Article 317 details the removal process of members.
- Article 320 defines the functions of the Commissions.
- UPSC was established on 1 October 1926 but received constitutional status on 26 January 1950.
- The Constitution also allows for a Joint Public Service Commission (JPSC) under Article 315(2) for two or more States.

question:
Article 39A of the Indian Constitution deals with:

[SSC GD 2024]
options: Right to life
Panchayati Raj
Right to freedom
Free legal aid
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Free legal aid

Explanation:
Article 39A of the Indian Constitution deals with free legal aid. It was inserted by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment, 1976 and is part of the Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP). Its objective is to ensure equal justice so that economically or socially disadvantaged groups can access justice. This article has been discussed in cases like Maneka Gandhi v. Union of India (1978), where the court linked it with Article 21 (Right to Life).

Extra Facts:
- Article 39A is implemented through the Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987.
- The National Legal Services Authority (NALSA) oversees its enforcement.
- It is part of Part IV of the Constitution (DPSP), which is non-justiciable but guides state policy-making.

question:
Which article of the Indian Constitution deals with the special address by the President to the parliament?

[NTPC CBT 2]
options: 87
81
79
85
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 87

Explanation:
Article 87 of the Indian Constitution deals with the special address by the President to both Houses of Parliament (Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha). This article provides for the President's address in two scenarios:
1. At the commencement of the first session after each general election to the Lok Sabha.
2. At the beginning of the first session each year (commonly referred to as the 'Budget Session').
In this address, the President outlines the government's policies, plans, and national priorities. This constitutional convention is inspired by the British parliamentary system.

Extra Facts:
- Article 86 empowers the President to address either House of Parliament or a joint sitting and send messages.
- Article 85 relates to sessions of Parliament, prorogation, and dissolution.
- The President's address is prepared by the government and delivered on the advice of the Council of Ministers (Article 74).
- Since 1950, the first parliamentary address by a President was delivered by Dr. Rajendra Prasad.

question:
Which Article of the Constitution explains that the executive power of every state shall be so exercised as not to impede or prejudice the exercise of the executive power of the Union, and the executive power of the union shall extend to the giving of such directions to a state as may appear to the Government of India to be necessary for that purpose?

[SSC CGL 2024]
options: Article 261
Article 247
Article 257
Article 123
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Article 257

Explanation:
Article 257 is part of Part XI (Union-State Relations) of the Indian Constitution. It mandates that the executive power of every state must be exercised in a manner that does not impede or prejudice the exercise of the executive power of the Union. Additionally, it empowers the Union government to issue necessary directions to states for national interest. This provision ensures coordination between the Centre and states in a federal structure.

Extra Facts:
◼ Article 256 directs states to ensure compliance with Union laws.
◼ Under Article 365, if a state fails to comply with Central directions, the President can declare a constitutional breakdown in the state.
◼ These provisions strengthen the federal structure and grant the Centre supervisory authority over states.

options_hi: अनुच्छेद 261
अनुच्छेद 247
अनुच्छेद 257
अनुच्छेद 123
solution_hi:
हल: सही उत्तर है अनुच्छेद 257

Explanation:
अनुच्छेद 257 भारतीय संविधान के भाग XI (संघ-राज्य संबंध) में शामिल है। यह अनुच्छेद स्पष्ट करता है कि राज्यों की कार्यकारी शक्ति का प्रयोग इस प्रकार किया जाएगा कि वह संघ (केंद्र सरकार) की कार्यकारी शक्ति के प्रयोग में बाधा या प्रतिकूल प्रभाव न डाले। इसके अलावा, यह केंद्र सरकार को यह अधिकार देता है कि वह राज्यों को आवश्यक निर्देश जारी कर सकती है, जो राष्ट्रीय हित में जरूरी हों। यह प्रावधान संघीय ढांचे में केंद्र और राज्यों के बीच सामंजस्य बनाए रखने के लिए महत्वपूर्ण है।

◼ ये प्रावधान संघीय ढांचे को मजबूत करते हैं और केंद्र को राज्यों पर नियंत्रण रखने की शक्ति प्रदान करते हैं।

question:
Which Clause of Article 20 incorporates the doctrine of double jeopardy?

[SSC CHSL 2024]
options: 3
2
1
4
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Clause 2

Explanation:
Article 20(2) of the Indian Constitution incorporates the 'Doctrine of Double Jeopardy'. It states that "No person shall be prosecuted and punished for the same offence more than once." This principle is inspired by the 'Fifth Amendment' of the US Constitution and ensures fairness in the Indian judicial system by preventing multiple trials and punishments for the same crime.

Extra Facts:
☛ Article 20 provides three fundamental protections:
1. Clause 1 – Protection against ex-post facto laws (no person shall be convicted for an act that was not an offence at the time of commission).
2. Clause 2 – Protection against double jeopardy.
3. Clause 3 – Protection against self-incrimination.
☛ This doctrine is part of Fundamental Rights (Part III) and can be enforced under Article 32.

☛ Article 20(3) safeguards against what? → Self-incrimination
☛ From which country's Constitution is the Double Jeopardy principle borrowed? → USA
☛ Under which Part is Article 20 located? → Part III (Fundamental Rights)
☛ Which clause of Article 20 protects against self-incrimination? → Clause 3

3. खंड 3 – स्वयं अपने विरुद्ध गवाही देने के विरुद्ध संरक्षण (Self-incrimination का निषेध)।

[RRB NTPC CBT]

Nagaland
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Nagaland

Explanation:
Article 371-A of the Indian Constitution provides special status to the state of Nagaland. This article was inserted through the 13th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1962. Under this provision, the Nagaland Legislative Assembly has special powers to make laws regarding land and resources. The Parliament also consults the state government before making laws on certain subjects related to Nagaland.

- Articles 371 to 371-J contain special provisions for various states (e.g., Maharashtra, Gujarat, Andhra Pradesh, etc.).

- यह अनुच्छेद नागा हिल्स-तुएनसांग क्षेत्र (अब नागालैंड) के लिए विशेष प्रावधान करता है।

question:
The Centre scrapped Article 370 of the Constitution in 2019. This article granted special status to ________ .

[SSC MTS 2022]
options: Uttar Pradesh
Punjab
Himachal Pradesh
Jammu and Kashmir
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Jammu and Kashmir

Explanation:
Article 370 of the Indian Constitution granted special status to Jammu and Kashmir. This provision was introduced under the 'Instrument of Accession' (1947), which provided the state with significant autonomy within the Indian Union. Under this article, the central government could legislate only on matters related to defense, foreign affairs, and communications, while other subjects were under the state's jurisdiction. On 5 August 2019, the Indian government revoked Article 370 through the Constitution (Application to Jammu and Kashmir) Order, 2019, thereby ending its special status. Subsequently, Jammu and Kashmir was reorganized into two Union Territories—Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh.

Extra Facts:
◼ Under Article 370, Jammu & Kashmir had its own constitution, flag, and administrative autonomy.
◼ Article 35A, a part of Article 370, empowered the state to define its permanent residents and grant them special rights.
◼ Post-revocation, all provisions of the Indian Constitution now apply to Jammu & Kashmir.
◼ The Jammu and Kashmir Reorganisation Act, 2019 was passed to bifurcate the state into two UTs.

[SSC CGL 2022]

Article 371
Article 371F
Article 371A
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Article 371F

Explanation:

It was inserted through the 36th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1975, which made Sikkim the 22nd state of India. This article contains provisions related to Sikkim’s Legislative Assembly, land laws, rights of its citizens, and other special arrangements, considering its historical and cultural uniqueness.

Extra Facts:

question:
Which Article of the Constitution of India lays down qualifications for the membership of the Parliament?

[SSC MTS 2024]
options: Article 105
Article 85
Article 84
Article 80
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Article 84

Explanation:
Article 84 of the Indian Constitution lays down the qualifications for membership of Parliament (Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha). According to it, a person must:
1. Be a citizen of India,
2. Be at least 25 years old for Lok Sabha and 30 years old for Rajya Sabha,
3. Fulfill other qualifications prescribed by Parliament.
Article 105 deals with parliamentary privileges, Article 85 relates to sessions of Parliament, prorogation, and dissolution, and Article 80 defines the composition of Rajya Sabha.

Extra Facts:
- Article 102 defines disqualifications for parliamentary membership, such as holding an office of profit, insolvency, or loss of citizenship.
- The Representation of the People Act, 1951 provides additional conditions, like disqualification if election security is forfeited.
- In the Lily Thomas Case (2013), the Supreme Court ruled that an MP’s election would be void if disqualified.

Which of the following is the constituent of article 182 of the Indian Constitution?

The Chairman and Deputy Chairman of the Legislative Council.
Vacation and resignation of, and removal from, the offices of chairman and Deputy Chairman.
solution:

Explanation:
Article 182 of the Indian Constitution deals with the Chairman and Deputy Chairman of the Legislative Council. This article specifies the election, functions, and removal process of the Chairman and Deputy Chairman in State Legislative Councils. It ensures the smooth functioning of the state legislatures.

Extra Facts:
- Article 183 covers the vacation of office, resignation, and removal of the Chairman and Deputy Chairman.
- Members of the Legislative Council elect the Chairman and Deputy Chairman from among themselves.
- Legislative Councils are constituted under Article 168 and exist only in a few states.

question:
The Supreme Court, in May 2023, observed that it can give divorce on the ground of irretrievable breakdown of marriage by exercising its discretionary power under_____.

[SSC CHSL 2024]
options: Article 142 of the Constitution of India
Article 143 of the Constitution of India
Article 32 of the Constitution of India
Article 136 of the Constitution of India
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Article 142 of the Constitution of India

Explanation:
The Supreme Court, in May 2023, exercised its discretionary power under Article 142 to grant divorce on the ground of irretrievable breakdown of marriage. Article 142 empowers the Supreme Court to pass any decree or order necessary for doing 'complete justice' in any case pending before it, where no specific provision exists under the Constitution or law. This article grants extraordinary powers to the Court to ensure justice, even in matrimonial disputes where reconciliation is impossible.

Extra Facts:
Article 142 has been invoked in landmark cases like the Bhopal Gas Tragedy (1989) for victim compensation, 2G Spectrum Case (2012) to cancel licenses, and Triple Talaq Case (2017) to declare instant divorce unconstitutional. It allows the Court to issue orders beyond legislative or executive jurisdiction to uphold justice. Notably, this power is unique to the Supreme Court and not available to High Courts.

question:
The High Court’s power to issue writs is mentioned under:

[NTPC CBT 2]
options:
Article 233

Article 226

Article 230

Article 225
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Article 226

Explanation:
The High Court's power to issue writs is mentioned under Article 226 of the Constitution of India. This article grants High Courts the authority to issue directions, orders, and writs such as habeas corpus, mandamus, prohibition, quo warranto, and certiorari to enforce both Fundamental Rights and any other legal right. 
Key aspects of Article 226:
Scope: The power under Article 226 extends to any person or authority, including government, within the High Court's jurisdiction. 
Two-fold purpose: It allows High Courts to issue writs not only for the enforcement of Fundamental Rights but also for any other legal right, which makes its jurisdiction broader than that of the Supreme Court. 
Types of Writs: The High Courts can issue the five main types of writs:
Habeas Corpus: To produce a person unlawfully detained. 
Mandamus: To order a person or authority to perform a public duty. 
Prohibition: To direct a lower court to stop proceedings on a case outside its jurisdiction. 
Quo Warranto: To question the legality of a person's claim to a public office. 
Certiorari: To review a decision made by a lower court.

question:

solution:

Explanation:
Article 129 of the Indian Constitution establishes the Supreme Court as a 'Court of Record'. This means that the judgments and proceedings of the Supreme Court are preserved as permanent records and can be cited as evidence in future cases. The article also empowers the Supreme Court to punish for contempt of itself. The significance of the Supreme Court being a Court of Record lies in ensuring judicial authority and transparency.

Extra Facts:
Apart from Article 129, Article 215 grants High Courts the status of a Court of Record. The records of the Supreme Court cannot be challenged in any court, as mentioned in Article 141. This provision helps maintain the dignity and fairness of the judicial process. As a Court of Record, the Supreme Court allows its judgments to be used as precedents by itself or other courts in the future.

solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 241

Explanation:
Article 241 of the Indian Constitution deals with High Courts for Union Territories. question:
Which article of the Indian Constitution guarantees ‘equality of opportunity’ in the matters of public employment?

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options: Article 17
Article 18
Article 15
Article 16
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Article 16

Explanation:
Article 16 of the Indian Constitution guarantees 'equality of opportunity' in matters of public employment. It prohibits discrimination in employment under the State on grounds of religion, race, caste, sex, descent, place of birth, or residence. However, Article 16(4) allows the State to provide reservations for backward classes. This provision was crucial in the Mandal Commission Case (1992), where the Supreme Court upheld a 50% cap on reservations.

Extra Facts:
- Article 15 prohibits discrimination based on religion, caste, sex, etc., but it deals with general equality, not specifically employment.
- Article 17 abolishes untouchability, while Article 18 abolishes titles.
- In the Indra Sawhney Case (1992), the Supreme Court ruled that reservations should not exceed 50%, except in extraordinary circumstances.

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options_hi: अनुच्छेद 17

solution_hi:

भारतीय संविधान का अनुच्छेद 16 सार्वजनिक रोजगार के मामलों में 'अवसर की समानता' की गारंटी देता है। यह अनुच्छेद राज्य के अधीन किसी भी पद पर नियोजन या नियुक्ति से संबंधित विभेदों को प्रतिबंधित करता है। इसमें धर्म, मूलवंश, जाति, लिंग, उद्भव, जन्म स्थान या निवास आदि के आधार पर भेदभाव न करने का प्रावधान है। हालांकि, अनुच्छेद 16(4) राज्य को पिछड़े वर्गों के लिए आरक्षण देने का अधिकार देता है। यह प्रावधान मंडल आयोग केस (1992) में 50% आरक्षण सीमा तय करने के लिए महत्वपूर्ण था।

Extra Facts:
- अनुच्छेद 15 धर्म, जाति, लिंग आदि के आधार पर भेदभाव को प्रतिबंधित करता है, लेकिन यह सामान्य समानता से संबंधित है, न कि विशेष रूप से रोजगार से।
- अनुच्छेद 17 अस्पृश्यता का उन्मूलन करता है, जबकि अनुच्छेद 18 उपाधियों का उन्मूलन करता है।
- इंदिरा साहनी केस (1992) में सर्वोच्च न्यायालय ने कहा कि आरक्षण 50% से अधिक नहीं होना चाहिए, जब तक कि असाधारण परिस्थितियाँ न हों।
